write_offs.reason: Without drop(guard) the guard is released at the end of SharedFrame::update_rect, right after mark_dirty, on the same thread; no pixel, damage, version or return value changes, and a woken render thread waits only that moment for the lock.
write_buf is resized to exactly `expected` bytes and the next line overwrites all of them from `data`, so the fill value of the resize is never read.

Without drop(guard) the guard is released at the end of SharedFrame::update_full, right after mark_dirty, on the same thread; nothing a caller reads changes, and a woken render thread waits only that moment for the lock.
